title: Singapore Retail Customer 360
thesis: On one governed platform, Snowflake turns aggregate daily activity from synthetic loyalty cohorts of Kopi Lane Retail, a fictional Singapore omnichannel retailer, into retention KPIs in SGD, 7-day churn risk per cohort, return rate anomalies and AI answers that cite their sources.

talking_points: 48 loyalty cohorts shop at Kopi Lane Retail malls and online in five Singapore planning areas: Orchard, Tampines, Jurong East, Woodlands and Punggol. The cards show issue-free purchase rate, service issues, churned members and revenue in SGD.
Each KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so you can trace it to cohort-day rows. No individual customer records are stored.
The issue-type chart separates issues that end in churn from ones that are always resolved, such as the mall checkout outages in Jurong East and Woodlands.
tabs.call_out: Customer KPIs you can trace to source rows

transition.line: Which cohorts need a retention review first?

talking_points: A Snowflake ML classifier estimates, per cohort, the chance of a churn event in the next 7 days.
Precision and recall come from the latest 14 labelled days held out of training, shown next to the base rate.
Anomaly detection picks out unusual cohort return rates, and the forecast covers the next 14 days of service issues.
tabs.call_out: ML that is evaluated honestly, next to the data

transition.line: Are we keeping in touch with every cohort?

talking_points: CRM touch compliance, profile completeness and pending profile fields show where engagement is slipping.
Plotting CRM touch compliance against churned members per cohort shows where the two move together; that is an association, not a cause.
The action memo proposes three prioritised actions using only the KPI, cohort, issue-type and risk rows.
show: CRM touch compliance and profile completeness
CRM touch compliance vs churned members
tabs.call_out: Draft actions grounded in data, reviewed by a person

transition.line: What happens when a member hits a problem right now?

talking_points: New engagement events arrive in RAW.LIVE_ENGAGEMENT, either from the simulator or from Amazon Data Firehose through Snowpipe.
The alert records each ISSUE event with an SOP hint and the risk band of the cohort, then emails the on-call retention analyst.
tabs.call_out: From a live service issue to a retention case on one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent answers metric questions with Cortex Analyst over the semantic view, and procedure questions with Cortex Search over 14 synthetic SOPs.
Every answer shows the SQL it generated and the SOP IDs it cited.
tabs.call_out: Answers in plain language that you can check

transition.line: This is how it fits together.

talking_points: One core supports two builds: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake with Data Firehose, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q.
All data shown is synthetic and aggregate, and rebuilds the same way from the repo.
tabs.call_out: A governed core with an optional AWS edge
